## Cloud credentials and API URL
\
n`--api-key` and `--api-url` are declared on `mcpjam cloud` and work before or after descendants (`mcpjam cloud --api-key sk_… eva
l list` and `mcpjam cloud eval list --api-key sk_…` are the same). Local commands, including hosted `readiness`, reject those flag

s at the program root. Hosted `readiness` still takes leaf `--api-key`.

Credential precedence for Cloud commands:

1. `--api-
key` — must be an `sk_` key. A `mcpjam_…` legacy key is a usage error.\n2. `MCPJAM_API_KEY` — same `sk_` rule. A legacy value in t
his env var is ignored (with a warning) so SDK eval reporting can still use it.\n3. Stored OAuth from `mcpjam cloud login`\n4. Mis
sing — Cloud commands fail with login guidance before they hit the network (`mcpjam cloud status` reports `missing` instead)\n\nAP

I URL precedence:

1. `--api-url`
2. `MCPJAM_API_URL`, or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` (the same server without `/api/v1`)
3. The server
saved with the OAuth login (only when that login is the credential; a login saved before logins recorded their server counts as MC
PJam Cloud, and one whose recorded server is not a usable address is refused with exit `3`)\n4. `https://app.mcpjam.com/api/v1`\n\
nEvery command that can contact MCPJam (it accepts `--api-url`, or it uploads results) decides its server when it starts, before i
t contacts anything. An explicit `--api-url`, `MCPJAM_API_URL` or `MCPJAM_BASE_URL` that is not an `http(s)` URL, or that carries
credentials, a query or a fragment, is a usage error (exit `2`), and so are the two variables naming different servers. The error
masks credentials, a query and a fragment, and does not repeat a value that is not a URL. A saved login is only sent to its own se
rver: when it is the credential and the order picks another server, the command exits `3` before any request. `mcpjam cloud status
` uses the same checks but stays network-free: it still emits the complete JSON report, sets `ok: false`, includes `credential.val
id` / `deployment.valid` plus an `error` string, and exits `1`. Missing credentials are informational (`credential.valid: null`) a
nd successful.\n\nSuccessful Cloud commands print an audience line to stderr (`Using MCPJam Cloud as … · project: … · <apiUrl>`).

`--quiet` suppresses it. Machine-readable JSON stays on stdout. `cloud status` redacts API keys.

# Local Evals

> Run an MCPJam eval suite file on your machine with mcpjam test with local results and an MCPJam identity

> [!NOTE]
>
>
The upcoming SDK 10, CLI 6, and Vitest 0.3 releases require an MCPJam login or `sk_` API key for every eval, including BYOK runs w
ith uploads disabled. These versions must ship after the backend run-start endpoint is deployed. Earlier versions keep their exist
ing behavior.\n\n`mcpjam test <file>` runs an MCPJam suite file locally: it connects your MCP servers, drives each case's prompts
through a model, grades the transcript with the same assertions a hosted run uses, and decides the run with the same verdict polic
y. Bring your own provider key and authenticate the run with MCPJam. With MCPJam-hosted inference it uses your existing CLI login
and billing.\n\nResults are **never uploaded**. The command writes results to your terminal and, if you ask, to a report file. It
records the run start with MCPJam. Like every command, it sends the CLI's single anonymous [telemetry](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli
/telemetry.md) event, which `--no-telemetry` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` turns off; the run adds no telemetry of its own.\n\n## Eval ident
ity and local data\n\nRun `mcpjam cloud login` locally, or set `MCPJAM_API_KEY` to an organization `sk_` key in CI. The SDK also a
ccepts `apiKey` or `mcpjamAuth` in run options. Explicit credentials take precedence over `MCPJAM_API_KEY`, which takes precedence
over the saved CLI login. An invalid explicit credential never falls back to another account. CI never starts an interactive logi
n. Ask an organization admin for a key if you cannot create one.\n\nEvery logical run needs an online start response. MCPJam retri
es transient failures within ten seconds, then stops before execution. A prior successful run does not enable offline execution. T
he CLI resolves the project using its existing `--project`, environment, and linked-project settings; a key can only access its ow
n organization.\n\nWith results uploads disabled, the start-run request sends only the credential in the authorization header, any
MCPJam API headers you configure through the SDK's `inference.resolveMcpjam`, project selection, a new run-start ID, client versi
on and surface (SDK, CLI, or Vitest), planned iteration count, provider names, and whether a client profile is used (`unknown` for
custom executors). The server resolves the organization and account. The start-run request sends no prompts, outputs, tool calls,
or server URLs. MCPJam-hosted inference still sends prompts through MCPJam to the model, as before. Retries reuse the same ID. Pl
anned iterations are intent, not completed usage or a charge. This release adds no debit, quota draw, or balance refusal.\n\n`DO_N
OT_TRACK`, `MCPJAM_TELEMETRY_DISABLED`, and CLI telemetry settings disable analytics, not the required run-start request. Results

remain local unless result uploading is enabled separately.

ay?
